prompt: Which statement best describes the Central Limit Theorem?

choices.label: The sample mean always equals the population mean when $n$ is large.
For large $n$, the sampling distribution of $\bar{x}$ is approximately normal, whatever the shape of the population.
Taking a large sample makes the population itself approximately normal.
The standard deviation of $\bar{x}$ grows as $n$ grows.

hint: The CLT is about the SHAPE of the distribution of sample means, not about the population or any single sample.

hints.text: The CLT is about the SHAPE of the distribution of sample means, not about the population or any single sample.
Rule out A (sample means still vary), C (the population does not change), and D (the SD of $\bar{x}$ shrinks with $n$).
B: with a large enough sample, sample means are approximately normal even from a skewed population.

explanation: The Central Limit Theorem says that as $n$ grows, the sampling distribution of $\bar{x}$ becomes approximately normal, regardless of the population's shape.
A is false because $\bar{x}$ gets close to $\mu$ but still varies. C is false because sampling does not change the population. D is backwards, since $\sigma_{\bar{x}} = \sigma/\sqrt{n}$ shrinks.
So B is the correct description of the theorem.

alternativeExplanations.title: Three different distributions
steps: Population distribution: all the individuals (any shape).
Distribution of one sample: looks roughly like the population.
Sampling distribution of $\bar{x}$: the one the CLT is about — bell-shaped for large $n$ (a common rule: $n \ge 30$).
